factor.name: Re-deployed to new addresses in last year
factor.scoring_methodology:
**What this measures**
This factor records whether the protocol redeployed to a new set of contract addresses in the trailing twelve months, retiring at least one previously-live contract that held user funds. Redeployments are detected via on-chain history and protocol announcements. This does not include proxy upgrades (which preserve the address), only full address migrations. It flags the risk that a migration introduced new, unaudited code or created a window during which user funds were briefly in a less-secure state.

**Why it matters**
Full redeployments are high-risk events for two related reasons. First, the new contracts are effectively new code that begins life with no battle-testing clock, resetting the age signal (RD-F-076). Second, redeployments often occur under operational pressure (post-exploit remediation, V2 launches) when the team's attention is divided and the temptation to skip re-audit is strongest. GMX V1 ($42M recovered, 2025) was exploited via a security patch added three years after the last audit -- a redeployment-style risk even without a full address migration. Several protocols in the dataset also exploited migration windows to front-run users moving funds to the new version.

**Green / Yellow / Red**
Green: no redeployment to new addresses in the trailing twelve months. Yellow: one redeployment with a full audit of the new contracts and public migration announcement with adequate lead time. Red: redeployment without a new audit of the migrated code, or redeployment with fewer than seventy-two hours of public notice to allow users to exit.

**Common gray cases**
Protocols that operate a perpetual multi-version architecture (V1 and V2 simultaneously live) are distinguished from full migrations; the score applies only to deployments intended to replace prior versions that held user funds.

**Notable historical examples**
No cross-hacked incidents currently linked in database for this factor.

scored_protocols.evidence_detail: The July 2025 TipRouter upgrade extended the existing system for priority-fee distributions; Jito describes it as a live upgrade and program extension, not retirement of JitoSOL to a replacement address set.
scored_protocols.evidence_summary: No full redeployment retiring JitoSOL to a new address set was identified in the trailing year. The July 2025 TipRouter change was a documented upgrade/extension, not a replacement migration.

scored_protocols.evidence_detail: The public repository identifies a stable mainnet program ID and its releases show continuing versioned development. This assessment found no announced retirement-and-redeployment of a user-fund-holding core address in the trailing year.
scored_protocols.evidence_summary: No public full migration to a new Kamino Lend mainnet program address was identified in the trailing year; the public deployment record continues to identify KLend2g3cP87fffoy8q1mQqGKjrxjC8boSyAYavgmjD as mainnet.
A complete public trailing-year record of full core address migrations was not available for verification.

Lombard's current smart-contract inventory identifies active deployments but does not publish a complete one-year retirement and replacement history. The reviewed public evidence cannot establish whether a prior address set was retired following a redeployment.

scored_protocols.evidence_detail: The official address inventory labels the listed legacy OUSG contracts as deprecated on dates through 2025-04-07 and lists the current contract set separately. No documented full protocol redeployment falls within the trailing twelve months.
scored_protocols.evidence_summary: No full redeployment to a new address set was identified in the trailing twelve months; the disclosed legacy migrations predate the window.

Pendle announced and started a governance/reward migration from vePENDLE to a newly deployed sPENDLE contract in January 2026. The announcement gave advance notice, and Pendle's developer documentation states the new contract was audited. This is a material new-address migration in the trailing year, so it is yellow rather than green; no evidence found supports an unaudited or unannounced migration.
